subject: Physics
topic: Why the sky is blue and sunsets are red
title: Why the Sky is Blue and Sunsets are Red
summary: Air scatters blue light far more than red. Blue fills the sky by day; at sunset the long path through the air removes the blue, and red and orange reach you.

notes.title: 01 – Why the Sky is Blue and Sunsets are Red

keyPoints: Blue (≈450 nm) scatters about 5–6 times more than red (≈700 nm).
Sunset: light crosses much more air, so the blue is scattered out on the way.
No atmosphere (the Moon): a black sky.

blocks.alt: Bar chart of scattering strength for violet, blue, green, yellow and red light
blocks.caption: Scattering ∝ 1/λ⁴, relative to red.

head: Term
Meaning
rows: Red is long (≈700 nm); blue is short (≈450 nm); violet is shortest (≈400 nm).
Scattering by particles much smaller than the wavelength, such as air molecules; strength ∝ 1/λ⁴.

list: Sunlight is white: it contains every colour.
Air molecules scatter short-wavelength blue far more than red.
Scattered blue reaches your eyes from every direction, so the whole sky looks blue.
Why not violet? Sunlight has less violet, some is absorbed high up, and our eyes are less sensitive to it.
At sunset the light crosses a much thicker layer of air; most blue is scattered out, so red and orange reach you.
Clouds are white: water droplets are much bigger than the wavelength and scatter all colours almost equally.
Danger signals are red: red is scattered least by fog and smoke, so it travels farthest.
The sky is blue over deserts too, so it is not a reflection of the ocean.

quiz.q: Which colour of visible light is scattered least by air?
quiz.explain: Scattering ∝ 1/λ⁴, and red has the longest wavelength.

quiz.q: Why would an astronaut on the Moon see a black sky?
options: There is no atmosphere to scatter sunlight
quiz.explain: No air means no scattering, so no light comes from the rest of the sky.

options: Light crosses much more air, so blue is scattered out
Red light is reflected by the sea
The Sun emits only red in the evening
quiz.explain: The Sun emits the same light; the longer path removes the blue.

options: They are made of ice only
Their droplets are big and scatter all colours almost equally
quiz.explain: Droplets much bigger than the wavelength scatter all colours about equally, so the mixture looks white.

simulation.reason: Moving the Sun and watching the same 1/λ⁴ rule turn the sky blue and the Sun red is a real cause-and-effect experiment students cannot do at home; the readouts make the longer path at sunset visible.
simulation.objective: See how the Sun's height changes the air the light crosses, and with it the colour of the Sun and the sky.
instructions: Drag the Sun-height slider from high to the horizon.
Watch the Sun and sky colours and the blue and red percentages that reach you.
Tick 'No atmosphere' to see the Moon's black sky.
